top_signal.title: Do I just give out the samples to retailers to attract them for sourcing?
top_signal.summary: Somehow with the tariff mess and fuel prices I have started to twist my ballgame a little to supplying for retailers. This seems to need to involve me actually working with a big distributor that some of them use. Well, supposedly the distributor expects my small company to find the retailers and get them on board first and then start using the distributor once the retailer agrees that they want some.   So, how do I open the eyes of the retailers to take interest in my branded product that is unique and you can't find on the market anywhere? Do I just bring a bunch of product into the USA and start giving out samples to merchandise outlets to sell as a sample run or something? Something makes me think a retailer has to already recognize that they were looking for a product before you came to them.   I mean, you can't just say that you have millions in sales and expect a merchandise outlet to automatically take interest. They may not even be looking for your type of product anyways.   I guess that's where my question comes from. How do I make them want it? They may not even know that they need this to pump their own business. Previous sales don't seem to matter here. They have to want to better themselves.   Any ideas on this? Just send them some samples to sell? That might even beat ad spend online for myself too so it could be better.   Thanks       submitted by     /u/Just_Wondering34       [link]       [comments]
